**Thousands flee as First Nations bear the brunt of Canada's wildfires**

DESCRIPTION: Wildfires spread across Canada, forcing thousands to flee their homes

SUMMARY: Wildfires in Canada have forced 2,182 people from their homes, with 13 First Nations under evacuation orders. The fires have destroyed homes and community buildings in some areas, and more than 900 are currently burning. The situation is most dire in Ontario, where seven First Nations have fled the 193 fires burning there.

TWEET: "Wildfires in Canada force thousands to flee their homes, with 13 First Nations under evacuation orders. The situation in Ontario is particularly dire, with 193 fires burning and seven First Nations forced to flee." ⚠️

TAGS: Canada wildfires, Indigenous communities, First Nations, evacuation orders, Ontario

BODY:
In the midst of raging wildfires, thousands of people have been forced to flee their homes in Canada, with devastating impacts for First Nations communities. The situation is most dire in Ontario, where seven First Nations have fled the 193 fires now burning there. More than 900 wildfires are currently burning throughout Canada, with 13 First Nations under evacuation orders that have forced 2,182 people from their homes.

## Devastating impacts on First Nations communities

The Namaygoosisagagun (Collins) First Nation watched one blaze largely destroy its entire community in less than an hour, forcing residents to flee by boat. Residents reported having only minutes to gather their belongings before homes were overtaken by the flames on Wednesday, and Anishinabek Nation Grand Council Chief Linda Debassige said in a statement that all community members have been accounted for pending a full assessment. The effects of the wildfires have been most pronounced in this community, with extensive damage and destruction to homes and community buildings.

## The extent of the crisis

The situation in Ontario is particularly dire, with 193 fires burning and seven First Nations forced to flee. Of the 903 fires burning as of Friday, 750 remained out of control, and 43 had started within the prior 24 hours. The effect has been greatest in Ontario, where the 193 fires have left many without access to basic necessities.

## Uncertain future for displaced communities

The wildfires have left many without access to basic necessities, and the long-term effects of the crisis remain uncertain. As the situation continues to unfold, it remains to be seen how the displaced communities will be supported in the wake of the disaster. The situation highlights the need for effective emergency preparedness and response measures to protect vulnerable communities.

[Exact Story Title](https://grist.org/indigenous/thousands-flee-as-first-nations-bear-the-brunt-of-canadas-wildfires/)
